open_points.subject: A09 rule 2 path placeholder handling
open_points.text: "every `{name}` in the path takes the input port of that name"
open_points.question: How exactly is `{name}` parsed in declared paths (valid name characters, escaped braces, unmatched braces, repeated placeholders), and which malformed forms make a binding non-invocable at proposal time?
options: Treat any `{...}` as a placeholder and reject unmatched/empty braces
Allow only placeholders matching input-port name syntax and reject all other brace usage
Do no structural placeholder validation at proposal time; fail only at send time
open_points.default_guess: Allow only well-formed placeholders that match declared input port names, and refuse malformed brace patterns at proposal time.

open_points.subject: A09 rule 5 transport outcome split
open_points.text: "'Nothing could be sent' holds only when the failure happened before the kernel wrote the first byte of the request; any failure after that, before a status line arrived, is 'may have been sent'."
open_points.question: If the HTTP stack cannot reliably tell whether the first request byte was written, which side of the table must be used?
options: Classify uncertain cases as 'nothing could be sent'
Classify uncertain cases as 'may have been sent'
open_points.default_guess: Classify uncertainty as 'may have been sent' (non-read => outcome_unknown, read => service_unreachable).

open_points.subject: A05 phase 9 reach check under guards
open_points.text: "at least one output of every function node reaches, through edges and nodes, a flow output or an operation node"
open_points.question: Does "reaches" mean purely structural graph reachability, or only reachability through at least one guard-enabled path that can actually fire?
options: Require at least one potentially enabled guard path
Require guaranteed production to a sink in all guard outcomes

open_points.subject: A14 rule 2 resume authority vs A10 rule 6 draft-write authority
open_points.text: A14 rule 2: "its authority is checked as it stands at the resume: its unused approval ... or a grant still active"; A10 rule 6: "A `draft-write` send records as its authority the FlowActivation M18 ..."
open_points.question: When resuming a `service_unreachable` `draft-write` element (not a post-`not_applied` resend), is FlowActivation sufficient authority without approval/grant?
options: Yes, resume uses FlowActivation authority for draft-write
No, resume requires approval/grant for all effectful resends
Use grant if present, else FlowActivation
open_points.default_guess: Yes—FlowActivation remains sufficient for draft-write resends except the explicit post-`not_applied` fresh-approval case.
